title: I built Fund Desk to make risk management easy.  My Absolute goal is to save as many people as possible from stupidly risky trades, absolutely remove the possibility of liquidation and allow you to put the focus back on finding good trades.
author: Ok-Cobbler2773

replies.author: Ok-Cobbler2773
replies.body: Hey there :) I don’t see why not! Can I ask what exchanges you or the general community prefer to use for stocks? I’ll investigate what’s possible from an API perspective.

replies.author: Different-Scale5419
replies.body: I don’t use any exchange.  I was interested whether it could be used for stocks. If so what exchanges would you recommend

replies.author: Ok-Cobbler2773
replies.body: Ok fair enough. I will look into a calculator-only mode but Fund Desk essentially integrates with your exchange (Bybit for the time being). This integration is needed for live trade data, pair searching, journaling, fees and automatic order placements.

replies.author: Different-Scale5419
replies.body: My brokerage is Charles Schwab. You would have to get an approval to hook up with them. Better yet a standalone exchange would be better

replies.author: Different-Scale5419
replies.body: US citizen here not interested in anything to do with cryptocurrency

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
running on the user's own machine with their own key should be your headline, well above no subscription. the people who would trust a risk tool with exchange keys are exactly the ones who will never hand them to a server.

position sizing people will use on day one. the journal is the hard part, because those get abandoned almost immediately unless the entry is already written by the time they look at it. are you filling it from the order automatically?

replies.author: Ok-Cobbler2773
replies.body:
Hey there! 

Really good point on the API key — I think you’re right. I originally treated local-only as more of a technical/privacy feature, but for the exact people I’m building this for it’s probably one of the biggest trust points.

And yep, that’s exactly the thinking with the journal. I don’t want people manually filling out a diary after every trade because realistically they’ll stop doing it.   
The trade data is captured automatically from Bybit, with the journal being there to add the context around it.

I appreciate the feedback 🫡

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: auto-capture from Bybit is the right half to automate. the context field will still go empty after a few weeks unless you ask for it the moment the position opens, while they've got a reason in their head. asking that evening is already too late.
